questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Monash because I wanted to experience new academic standards while also living in a completely different culture. The combination of strong teaching, international peers, and the chance to challenge myself both academically and personally made Melbourne the ideal destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My exchange semester has been one of the best experiences of my studies. I learned a lot academically, met incredible people, and grew personally from living so far from home. I’m genuinely grateful for the opportunity.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Both KU and Monash were very helpful throughout the process, so it was easy to find the information I needed. And whenever I contacted Monash by email, they always found a solution to any problem.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Monash helped me get into all the systems, platforms, and practical setups I needed, which made the start smooth.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I can recommend Monash University

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was super easy to find housing through Airbnb. I would definitely recommend looking there first.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living in Southbank was amazing, and I would really recommend staying in the city rather than on campus. Many courses are either online or have recorded lectures, so you don’t need to be on campus every day. It gives you much more freedom and a much better experience of Melbourne.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I recommend living with other students from your home university — it makes everything easier and more fun.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just sent my pre-approval to Monash, and then I was registered in the correct courses. It was a very easy and simple process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Monash has a dedicated department for exchange students, so they can help with all the practical and more complicated parts of the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I received credit for all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write to the professors at Monash early and make sure you get all the information you need about the courses. KU requires a lot of documentation to approve them, and the process takes time — so start as early as possible

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A very solid academic system that still allows plenty of free time outside of university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses in Australia are generally very manageable, so if you come from KU, you are more than prepared for the academic level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is quite similar to UCPH, but Monash often has mandatory attendance. Grades are also typically based on a mix of assignments, presentations, participation, and a final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Macroeconomics (Makro III)
Game Theory and Strategic Thinking (Mikro III)
International Economics (Valgfag)
The Economic History of The Modern World (økonomisk historie)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All courses above

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing major — mainly small practical expenses that added up

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and eating out were cheaper than I expected, and public transport was also very affordable. Alcohol, however, was quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not attend any, so I don’t know.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Monash hosts many social events and activities throughout the semester, so there’s plenty to join if you want to meet people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just explore whatever you feel like — there’s a lot to experience, and Melbourne has something for everyone.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Great Ocean Road and the nightlife in Melbourne

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, especially because I travelled with four close friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and go out for a beer — Australians are easy to talk to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really. Australians are very open and welcoming.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness and friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Travel with people you know from KU — it makes the experience much better and less lonely. Don’t spend all your time on school; make sure to enjoy Melbourne and the culture as well. And definitely travel after the semester ends — it finishes early, so you have plenty of time before KU starts again.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Travel with someone you know

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the whole exchange together with my close friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Can’t really think of any.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
